Maintenance Report — MNT-0062-003

Asset: WELL-0062 (SW-24 Well 062, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 17 Feb 2023 08:00 · Finished: 17 Feb 2023 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0062-0018 on 2023-02-16 Report written: 18 Feb 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0062-0018 at 08:45 on 2023-02-16 found crude oil on the pad: about 4.1% of the pad area, estimated 1.1 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 5.5 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 242 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 194 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.4 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0062-003 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.31% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0062-007

Asset: WELL-0062 (SW-24 Well 062, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: separator Work started: 26 Aug 2023 08:00 · Finished: 13 Sep 2023 22:00 · Well stopped for this job: 446 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward, Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0062-0044 on 2023-08-24 Report written: 15 Sep 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the separator high-level alarm stayed on. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0062-0044 showed the wellhead at 36.3 °C with the air at 36.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The level controller had failed. The well stayed shut in for about 17 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Paraffin build-up stopped the float from moving.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Isolated and depressurised the separator.
  2. Replaced the level controller.
  3. Calibrated the controller and tested the dump valve.

Summary of the fix: replaced level controller.

Testing and return to service

Cycled the separator three times; level control worked correctly. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0062-021

Asset: WELL-0062 (SW-24 Well 062, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 30 Nov 2025 08:00 · Finished: 09 Dec 2025 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 220 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price, Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0062-0161 on 2025-11-27 Report written: 10 Dec 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0062-0161 showed the wellhead at 16.1 °C with the air at 11.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 7 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

Notes and recommendations

  • Clean the motor cooling fins at each scheduled service.
  • Summer heat raises the risk of motor trips on this field.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0062-025

Asset: WELL-0062 (SW-24 Well 062, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 07 Jun 2026 08:00 · Finished: 24 Jun 2026 22:00 · Well stopped for this job: 422 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0062-0188 on 2026-06-04 Report written: 24 Jun 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0062-0188 showed the wellhead at 36.5 °C with the air at 35.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 16 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 6 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 242 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 194 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0062-025 (WS-06).
